Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 23, verses 1–11:

Makkiyya (Meccan). It contains 4,802 letters, 1,840 words, and 118 verses.

Abu al-Hasan al-Khabbari informed us, saying: Ibn Habash related to us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Musa al-Daqqaq al-Razi related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Rawh al-Madaini related to us, saying: And Tafran related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Dawud related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Asim related to us, saying: Nassaba ibn Sawwar al-Fazari related to us, saying: Makhlad ibn Abd al-Wahid related to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Ata ibn Abi Maymuna, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Mu'minun, the angels will give him good news of ar-rawh (rest/mercy) and ar-rayhan (provision) and that which will delight his eye at the descent of the Angel of Death." [8] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 7/175.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Surely the believers have prospered.﴾ Qad is an emphatic particle. The muhaqqiqun (verifying scholars) said: the meaning of qad here is bringing the past close to the present, indicating that their success has already been attained and they are in that state now. This is more eloquent in description than stating the success without qad. Al-falah (success) means triumph and permanence.

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Mufassir informed us, by reading to me in the year 388 [AH], saying: Abu Amr al-Mu'tazz ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Qadi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Firyabi related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahim ibn Habib al-Baghdadi related to us, from Ishaq ibn Najih al-Malati, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah, glorified is He, created the Garden of Eden, He created in it what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Then He said to it: Speak. It said: ﴿Surely the believers have prospered﴾ three times. Then it said: I am forbidden to every miser and show-off." [9] [[Tarikh Madinat Dimashq: 52/151.]]

Talha ibn Musarrif recited: ﴿qad uflih al-mu'minun﴾ in the passive voice, meaning: they were granted continuance in reward.

﴿Who are humble in their prayer.﴾ The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of khushu'. Ibn Abbas said: humbled and submissive. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: fearful.

Muqatil said: humbly submissive, with the humility of the heart, and that you soften your side (kanf) toward the Muslim person and do not turn your attention away.

Mujahid said: it is lowering the gaze and lowering the wing (humility). A man of knowledge, when he stood to pray, would be awed before the Most Merciful, so that he would not extend his gaze to anything or let his soul dwell on any matter of worldly affairs.

Amr ibn Dinar said: khushu' is not merely bowing and prostrating, but rather stillness and good bearing in the prayer.

Ibn Sirin and others said: it is that you do not raise your gaze from the place of your prostration.

They said: The Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions used to raise their eyes to the sky during prayer and look right and left, until this verse was revealed, after which they placed their faces where they prostrate, and no one was seen afterward looking except at the ground.

Rabi' said: it is not turning right or left.

Abu Amr al-Furati informed us, saying: Abu Musa informed us, saying: al-Sarraj related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: Ibrahim al-Khawzi related to us, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, who said: I heard Abu Hurayra say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when the servant stands to pray, he is between the two eyes of the Most Merciful, the Mighty and Majestic. When he turns, the Lord says to him: To whom are you turning? To one better for you than Me? Son of Adam, come to Me, for I am better than the one you turn to." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 7/505.]]

Ata: it is not playing with any part of your body during prayer.

The Prophet (ﷺ) saw a man fidgeting with his beard in prayer and said: "If this man's heart were humbled, his limbs would be humbled." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 3/144.]]

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Uqayl al-Qattan informed us, saying: Sahib ibn Ahmad ibn Tarahhum ibn Sufyan informed us, saying: Abu Abd al-Rahman ibn Nabit al-Marwazi Abdan related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Ma'mar, that he heard al-Zuhri narrate from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you stands to pray, mercy faces him, so let him not move the pebbles." [10] [[al-Musannaf: 2/38.]]

It is related that al-Hasan saw a man playing with pebbles and saying: "O Allah, marry me to the wide-eyed houris." He said: "What a poor suitor you are! You are proposing while you are playing."

Khulayd [in the second copy: Khalil] ibn Da'laj, from Qatada: it is placing the right hand upon the left in prayer.

Some of them said: it is gathering one's resolve toward it and turning away from all else.

Abu Bakr al-Wasiti said: it is praying to Allah, glorified is He, with sincerity, without any compensation.

I heard Ibn al-Imam say: I heard Ibn Muqsim say: I heard Abu al-Fadl Ja'far ibn Ahmad al-Saydalani say: I heard Ibn Abi al-Ward say: The one who prays needs four qualities in order to be humble:

Magnifying the station, sincerity of speech, perfect certainty, and gathering of resolve.

﴿And who turn away from idle talk.﴾ Al-Hasan said: from sins. Ibn Abbas: false oaths. Muqatil: abuse and harm. Others: what is useless of speech and deed. It was also said: al-laghw is an action that has no benefit.

﴿And who are active in zakat.﴾ Fa'iluna: those who pay (muaddun), and this is eloquent usage, found in the speech of the Arabs. Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt said:

"The feeders of food in the year of drought... and the performers of the zakat."

﴿And who guard their private parts, except before their spouses or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy.﴾ Illa ala azwajihim means: from their spouses; ala here carries the sense of min, and aw ma is in the place of the genitive, meaning: or from what their right hands possess, concerning intercourse with their wives and their female slaves.

﴿But whoever seeks beyond that, it is they who are the transgressors.﴾ That is, whoever seeks and desires other than his wife and what his right hand possesses; those are the transgressors from the lawful to the unlawful. So whoever commits fornication is a transgressor.

﴿And who are faithful to their trusts and their covenants.﴾ Trusts (amanat) are what they were entrusted with, and covenants ('ahd) are the agreements they made with people; ra'un means guarding and fulfilling.

Ibn Kathir recited: li-amanatihim (singular), based on His saying: "and his covenant." The others recited it in the plural, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners﴾ [[Surat al-Nisa': 58.]].

﴿And who guard their prayers.﴾ They persist in performing them and observe their times. He commanded guarding them as He commanded humility in them, so He repeated the mention of prayer.

﴿Those are the inheritors﴾: the people of this description are the inheritors on the Day of Resurrection of the dwellings of the people of Paradise in the Garden.

Abu Hurayra related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "There is none of you but has a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in Hellfire. If he dies and enters the Fire, the people of Paradise inherit his dwelling. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Those are the inheritors﴾." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 2/8.]]

Mujahid said: Each one has two dwellings: a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. As for the believer, his dwelling that is in Paradise is built up, and his dwelling that is in the Fire is demolished. As for the disbeliever, his dwelling that is in Paradise is demolished, and his dwelling that is in the Fire is built up.

Some of them said: the meaning of inheritance is that their affair ends up in Paradise and they attain it, just as the matter of inheritance passes to the heir.

﴿Who will inherit al-Firdaws.﴾ Al-Firdaws means the garden, the abundant orchard. Mujahid said: it is in Roman (Greek) language. Ikrima said: it is the Garden in the language of the Abyssinians. Al-Suddi said: it is orchards enclosed by walls, in the language of the Romans.

In a hadith [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/215, with variation.]]: that Haritha ibn Suraqa was killed on the day of Badr, and his mother said: "O Messenger of Allah, if my son is among the people of Paradise, I will not weep for him; and if he is among the people of the Fire, I will weep greatly." He said: "O mother of Haritha, indeed there are gardens, and your son has attained the highest Firdaws of Paradise." [11]

Abu al-Hasan [in the second copy: Abu al-Abbas] Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Tabarani informed me there, saying: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yunus ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Nadr al-Muqri related to us, saying: al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl al-Muqri related to us, saying:

Abu Zur'a Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Karim related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Bukayr al-Makhzumi related to us, saying:

Ibn Lahi'a al-Hadrami related to me, saying: Ata ibn Dinar related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿Surely the believers have prospered﴾, meaning: those who affirm the Tawhid of Allah, glorified is He, have been made happy. Then He described them and their deeds, saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Who are humble in their prayer﴾, meaning: humbled, so that one does not know who is on his right or his left, and does not turn from humility before Allah. ﴿And who turn away from idle talk﴾, meaning: falsehood and lying. ﴿And who are active in zakat﴾, meaning: wealth, like His saying in al-A'la: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies himself﴾, meaning: from his wealth. ﴿And who guard their private parts﴾, meaning: from immorality. Then He said: ﴿except before their spouses or what their right hands possess﴾, meaning: their slave-women, ﴿for they are not blameworthy﴾, not to be blamed for intercourse with their spouses and slave-women. ﴿But whoever seeks beyond that﴾, so whoever seeks immorality after the spouses and slave-women, what is not lawful, ﴿it is they who are the transgressors﴾, meaning: those who exceed bounds in their religion. ﴿And who are faithful to their trusts﴾, meaning: what they are entrusted with between themselves and people, ﴿and their covenants they uphold﴾, meaning: guarding, rendering trusts and fulfilling covenants. ﴿And who guard their prayers﴾, meaning: they guard them at their appointed times. Then He informed of their reward, saying: ﴿Those are the inheritors﴾, then He explained what they inherit, saying: ﴿who will inherit al-Firdaws﴾, meaning: the Garden, in the Roman language, ﴿they will abide therein forever﴾, not dying therein.

Muhammad [in the second copy an addition: ibn Ahmad] ibn Uqayl al-Qattan [in the second copy: al-Attar] informed us, saying: Hajib ibn Ahmad ibn Sufyan informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hammad al-Bayurdi related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Sulaym informed me, saying: Sahib Ayla dictated to me [in the second copy an addition: Yunus ibn], from Ibn Shihab, from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd al-Qari, who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, say: When revelation descended upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a sound like the humming of bees was heard near his face. We remained for a while, then he faced the qibla, raised his hands and said: "O Allah, increase us and do not diminish us, honor us and do not humiliate us, give us and do not deprive us, prefer us and do not prefer others over us, and be pleased with us." Then he said: "Ten verses have been revealed to us; whoever establishes them will enter Paradise," then he recited: ﴿Surely the believers have prospered﴾ — ten verses. [[Muntakhab Musnad Abd ibn Humayd: p. 34.]] [12]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Mu'minun, the angels will give him good news of ar-rawh (rest/mercy) and ar-rayhan (provision) and that which will delight his eye at the descent of the Angel of Death." [8] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 7/175.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Surely the believers have prospered.﴾ Qad is an emphatic particle. The muhaqqiqun (verifying scholars) said: the meaning of qad here is bringing the past close to the present, indicating that their success has already been attained and they are in that state now. This is more eloquent in description than stating the success without qad. Al-falah (success) means triumph and permanence.

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Mufassir informed us, by reading to me in the year 388 [AH], saying: Abu Amr al-Mu'tazz ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Qadi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Firyabi related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahim ibn Habib al-Baghdadi related to us, from Ishaq ibn Najih al-Malati, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah, glorified is He, created the Garden of Eden, He created in it what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Then He said to it: Speak. It said: ﴿Surely the believers have prospered﴾ three times. Then it said: I am forbidden to every miser and show-off." [9] [[Tarikh Madinat Dimashq: 52/151.]]

Talha ibn Musarrif recited: ﴿qad uflih al-mu'minun﴾ in the passive voice, meaning: they were granted continuance in reward.

﴿Who are humble in their prayer.﴾ The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of khushu'. Ibn Abbas said: humbled and submissive. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: fearful.

Muqatil said: humbly submissive, with the humility of the heart, and that you soften your side (kanf) toward the Muslim person and do not turn your attention away.

Mujahid said: it is lowering the gaze and lowering the wing (humility). A man of knowledge, when he stood to pray, would be awed before the Most Merciful, so that he would not extend his gaze to anything or let his soul dwell on any matter of worldly affairs.

Amr ibn Dinar said: khushu' is not merely bowing and prostrating, but rather stillness and good bearing in the prayer.

Ibn Sirin and others said: it is that you do not raise your gaze from the place of your prostration.

They said: The Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions used to raise their eyes to the sky during prayer and look right and left, until this verse was revealed, after which they placed their faces where they prostrate, and no one was seen afterward looking except at the ground.

Rabi' said: it is not turning right or left.

Abu Amr al-Furati informed us, saying: Abu Musa informed us, saying: al-Sarraj related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: Ibrahim al-Khawzi related to us, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, who said: I heard Abu Hurayra say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when the servant stands to pray, he is between the two eyes of the Most Merciful, the Mighty and Majestic. When he turns, the Lord says to him: To whom are you turning? To one better for you than Me? Son of Adam, come to Me, for I am better than the one you turn to." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 7/505.]]

Ata: it is not playing with any part of your body during prayer.

The Prophet (ﷺ) saw a man fidgeting with his beard in prayer and said: "If this man's heart were humbled, his limbs would be humbled." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 3/144.]]

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Uqayl al-Qattan informed us, saying: Sahib ibn Ahmad ibn Tarahhum ibn Sufyan informed us, saying: Abu Abd al-Rahman ibn Nabit al-Marwazi Abdan related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Ma'mar, that he heard al-Zuhri narrate from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you stands to pray, mercy faces him, so let him not move the pebbles." [10] [[al-Musannaf: 2/38.]]

It is related that al-Hasan saw a man playing with pebbles and saying: "O Allah, marry me to the wide-eyed houris." He said: "What a poor suitor you are! You are proposing while you are playing."

Khulayd [in the second copy: Khalil] ibn Da'laj, from Qatada: it is placing the right hand upon the left in prayer.

Some of them said: it is gathering one's resolve toward it and turning away from all else.

Abu Bakr al-Wasiti said: it is praying to Allah, glorified is He, with sincerity, without any compensation.

I heard Ibn al-Imam say: I heard Ibn Muqsim say: I heard Abu al-Fadl Ja'far ibn Ahmad al-Saydalani say: I heard Ibn Abi al-Ward say: The one who prays needs four qualities in order to be humble:

Magnifying the station, sincerity of speech, perfect certainty, and gathering of resolve.

﴿And who turn away from idle talk.﴾ Al-Hasan said: from sins. Ibn Abbas: false oaths. Muqatil: abuse and harm. Others: what is useless of speech and deed. It was also said: al-laghw is an action that has no benefit.

﴿And who are active in zakat.﴾ Fa'iluna: those who pay (muaddun), and this is eloquent usage, found in the speech of the Arabs. Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt said:

"The feeders of food in the year of drought... and the performers of the zakat."

﴿And who guard their private parts, except before their spouses or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy.﴾ Illa ala azwajihim means: from their spouses; ala here carries the sense of min, and aw ma is in the place of the genitive, meaning: or from what their right hands possess, concerning intercourse with their wives and their female slaves.

﴿And who guard their prayers.﴾ They persist in performing them and observe their times. He commanded guarding them as He commanded humility in them, so He repeated the mention of prayer.

﴿Those are the inheritors﴾: the people of this description are the inheritors on the Day of Resurrection of the dwellings of the people of Paradise in the Garden.

Abu Hurayra related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "There is none of you but has a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in Hellfire. If he dies and enters the Fire, the people of Paradise inherit his dwelling. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Those are the inheritors﴾." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 2/8.]]

Mujahid said: Each one has two dwellings: a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. As for the believer, his dwelling that is in Paradise is built up, and his dwelling that is in the Fire is demolished. As for the disbeliever, his dwelling that is in Paradise is demolished, and his dwelling that is in the Fire is built up.

Some of them said: the meaning of inheritance is that their affair ends up in Paradise and they attain it, just as the matter of inheritance passes to the heir.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Mu'minun, the angels will give him good news of ar-rawh (rest/mercy) and ar-rayhan (provision) and that which will delight his eye at the descent of the Angel of Death." [8] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 7/175.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Surely the believers have prospered.﴾ Qad is an emphatic particle. The muhaqqiqun (verifying scholars) said: the meaning of qad here is bringing the past close to the present, indicating that their success has already been attained and they are in that state now. This is more eloquent in description than stating the success without qad. Al-falah (success) means triumph and permanence.

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Mufassir informed us, by reading to me in the year 388 [AH], saying: Abu Amr al-Mu'tazz ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Qadi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Firyabi related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahim ibn Habib al-Baghdadi related to us, from Ishaq ibn Najih al-Malati, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah, glorified is He, created the Garden of Eden, He created in it what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Then He said to it: Speak. It said: ﴿Surely the believers have prospered﴾ three times. Then it said: I am forbidden to every miser and show-off." [9] [[Tarikh Madinat Dimashq: 52/151.]]

Talha ibn Musarrif recited: ﴿qad uflih al-mu'minun﴾ in the passive voice, meaning: they were granted continuance in reward.

﴿Who are humble in their prayer.﴾ The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of khushu'. Ibn Abbas said: humbled and submissive. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: fearful.

Muqatil said: humbly submissive, with the humility of the heart, and that you soften your side (kanf) toward the Muslim person and do not turn your attention away.

Mujahid said: it is lowering the gaze and lowering the wing (humility). A man of knowledge, when he stood to pray, would be awed before the Most Merciful, so that he would not extend his gaze to anything or let his soul dwell on any matter of worldly affairs.

Amr ibn Dinar said: khushu' is not merely bowing and prostrating, but rather stillness and good bearing in the prayer.

Ibn Sirin and others said: it is that you do not raise your gaze from the place of your prostration.

They said: The Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions used to raise their eyes to the sky during prayer and look right and left, until this verse was revealed, after which they placed their faces where they prostrate, and no one was seen afterward looking except at the ground.

Rabi' said: it is not turning right or left.

Abu Amr al-Furati informed us, saying: Abu Musa informed us, saying: al-Sarraj related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: Ibrahim al-Khawzi related to us, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, who said: I heard Abu Hurayra say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when the servant stands to pray, he is between the two eyes of the Most Merciful, the Mighty and Majestic. When he turns, the Lord says to him: To whom are you turning? To one better for you than Me? Son of Adam, come to Me, for I am better than the one you turn to." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 7/505.]]

Ata: it is not playing with any part of your body during prayer.

The Prophet (ﷺ) saw a man fidgeting with his beard in prayer and said: "If this man's heart were humbled, his limbs would be humbled." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 3/144.]]

Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Uqayl al-Qattan informed us, saying: Sahib ibn Ahmad ibn Tarahhum ibn Sufyan informed us, saying: Abu Abd al-Rahman ibn Nabit al-Marwazi Abdan related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Ma'mar, that he heard al-Zuhri narrate from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you stands to pray, mercy faces him, so let him not move the pebbles." [10] [[al-Musannaf: 2/38.]]

It is related that al-Hasan saw a man playing with pebbles and saying: "O Allah, marry me to the wide-eyed houris." He said: "What a poor suitor you are! You are proposing while you are playing."

Khulayd [in the second copy: Khalil] ibn Da'laj, from Qatada: it is placing the right hand upon the left in prayer.

Some of them said: it is gathering one's resolve toward it and turning away from all else.

Abu Bakr al-Wasiti said: it is praying to Allah, glorified is He, with sincerity, without any compensation.

I heard Ibn al-Imam say: I heard Ibn Muqsim say: I heard Abu al-Fadl Ja'far ibn Ahmad al-Saydalani say: I heard Ibn Abi al-Ward say: The one who prays needs four qualities in order to be humble:

Magnifying the station, sincerity of speech, perfect certainty, and gathering of resolve.

﴿And who turn away from idle talk.﴾ Al-Hasan said: from sins. Ibn Abbas: false oaths. Muqatil: abuse and harm. Others: what is useless of speech and deed. It was also said: al-laghw is an action that has no benefit.

﴿And who are active in zakat.﴾ Fa'iluna: those who pay (muaddun), and this is eloquent usage, found in the speech of the Arabs. Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt said:

"The feeders of food in the year of drought... and the performers of the zakat."

﴿And who guard their private parts, except before their spouses or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy.﴾ Illa ala azwajihim means: from their spouses; ala here carries the sense of min, and aw ma is in the place of the genitive, meaning: or from what their right hands possess, concerning intercourse with their wives and their female slaves.

﴿But whoever seeks beyond that, it is they who are the transgressors.﴾ That is, whoever seeks and desires other than his wife and what his right hand possesses; those are the transgressors from the lawful to the unlawful. So whoever commits fornication is a transgressor.

﴿And who are faithful to their trusts and their covenants.﴾ Trusts (amanat) are what they were entrusted with, and covenants ('ahd) are the agreements they made with people; ra'un means guarding and fulfilling.

Ibn Kathir recited: li-amanatihim (singular), based on His saying: "and his covenant." The others recited it in the plural, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners﴾ [[Surat al-Nisa': 58.]].

﴿And who guard their prayers.﴾ They persist in performing them and observe their times. He commanded guarding them as He commanded humility in them, so He repeated the mention of prayer.

﴿Those are the inheritors﴾: the people of this description are the inheritors on the Day of Resurrection of the dwellings of the people of Paradise in the Garden.

Abu Hurayra related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "There is none of you but has a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in Hellfire. If he dies and enters the Fire, the people of Paradise inherit his dwelling. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Those are the inheritors﴾." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 2/8.]]

Mujahid said: Each one has two dwellings: a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. As for the believer, his dwelling that is in Paradise is built up, and his dwelling that is in the Fire is demolished. As for the disbeliever, his dwelling that is in Paradise is demolished, and his dwelling that is in the Fire is built up.

Some of them said: the meaning of inheritance is that their affair ends up in Paradise and they attain it, just as the matter of inheritance passes to the heir.

﴿Who will inherit al-Firdaws.﴾ Al-Firdaws means the garden, the abundant orchard. Mujahid said: it is in Roman (Greek) language. Ikrima said: it is the Garden in the language of the Abyssinians. Al-Suddi said: it is orchards enclosed by walls, in the language of the Romans.

In a hadith [[Musnad Ahmad: 3/215, with variation.]]: that Haritha ibn Suraqa was killed on the day of Badr, and his mother said: "O Messenger of Allah, if my son is among the people of Paradise, I will not weep for him; and if he is among the people of the Fire, I will weep greatly." He said: "O mother of Haritha, indeed there are gardens, and your son has attained the highest Firdaws of Paradise." [11]

Abu Zur'a Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Karim related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Bukayr al-Makhzumi related to us, saying:

Ibn Lahi'a al-Hadrami related to me, saying: Ata ibn Dinar related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning the saying of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿Surely the believers have prospered﴾, meaning: those who affirm the Tawhid of Allah, glorified is He, have been made happy. The common readers recited "munzalan mubārakan" with a damma on the mim, as a verbal noun, meaning "a blessed disembarking." 'Asim, in the transmission of Abu Bakr, recited it with a fatha on the mim and a kasra on the zay, meaning "a place" (of landing).

﴿Indeed, in that are signs. And indeed, We have always been testing [people].﴾ It was said: "wa-in kunnā" means "wa-qad kunnā" (indeed We have been), and it was said: "wa-mā kunnā illā mublīn" means: We were only testing and examining them by reminding them and admonishing them, so that We might see what they would do before the punishment descended upon them.

Will you not then fear [God]?"﴾

﴿The chiefs of his people who disbelieved and denied the meeting of the Hereafter, and whom We had given luxury in the life of this world, said: "This is none but a human being like you, who eats of what you eat and drinks of what you drink. The flesh has gone from the bones. "Annakum mukhrajūn" means: [you will be brought forth] from your graves alive. He repeated "innakum" because the speech had become long. The meaning of "wa-kuntum turāban wa-'izāman" (and you have become dust and bones) is: "innakum mukhrajūn" (you will be brought forth).
[[In the second copy (Isfahan): The meaning of the speech is: "Does he promise you that when you have died and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth?" It is mentioned that this is from the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud): "Does he promise you, when you have died and become dust and bones, that you will be brought forth?"]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 23, verses 36–44:

All of these are valid dialectal forms. Whoever uses the fatha treats it like "ayna" (where) and "kayfa" (how). It has also been said that, since they are two particles, they became like "khamsata 'ashara" (fifteen) and "Ba'labakk" (Baalbek) and the like.

Al-Farra' said: their fatha is like the fatha in the phrases "thumma" and "rubba." Whoever uses the damma treats it like "mundhu," "qatt" and "haythu," and whoever uses the kasra treats it like "ams" and "ha'ulaa'." A poet said:

*I remembered days that passed of my youth,*
*and "Far, far" is their return to you.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 12/122.]]

Another said:

*Umm al-Hamaris has distanced her dwelling,*
*and far is Umm al-Hamaris, far indeed.*

They differed concerning how to pause on it. Al-Kisa'i paused on it with a haa' and al-Farra' with a taa'. The lam was added to "hayhat" within the noun because it is a particle not derived from a verb, so they added the lam to it as they added it to "halumma lak."

﴿He said: "My Lord, help me, for they have denied me."﴾ ﴿He said: "In a little while they will surely become regretful"﴾ — "'amma qalil" means "after a little," and "ma" is a connecting particle — over their disbelief.

﴿Then We produced after them other generations.﴾ "Qarn" means the people of an era; they were so called because some are contemporaries of others (muqaranah).

Whoever uses tanwin pauses on it with an alif, and whoever does not use tanwin pauses on it with a ya'. It is also said that it is not a ya' but an alif with imalah. The common reciters recited it without tanwin, like "ghadabaa" and "sakraa"; it is a plural noun like "shatta." Its origin is "watra," from al-mawatarah and al-tawatur; the waw was changed to a taa' as in "al-taqwa" and "al-takalan" and the like.

﴿Every time a nation came to them with its messenger, they denied him, so We caused some of them to follow others﴾ — with destruction; that is, We destroyed some of them right after others.

﴿And We made them tales (ahadith)﴾ — that is, examples by which people speak. It is the plural of "uhdutha," and it may be the plural of "hadith." Al-Akhfash said: this is said only of evil; as for good, one does not say "We made them ahadith" or "uhdutha," but rather "so-and-so became a hadith."

﴿So away with a people who do not believe.﴾ Its parallel is in: ﴿And We made them tales and tore them completely apart﴾ [[Surat Saba': 19.]] ?

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 23, verse 45–59:

Then We sent Musa and his brother Harun with Our signs and a clear authority, to Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his chiefs. But they behaved arrogantly, [i.e., they magnified themselves against faith], and they were a haughty people [i.e., arrogant, subduing others through oppression]. Its parallel is ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land﴾ [Surah al-Qasas: 4].

﴿They said﴾ — meaning Fir'awn and his people — ﴿Shall we believe in two mortals like us, when their people are servants to us?﴾ — obedient and submissive. The Arabs call everyone who submits to a king an ʿabid (servant) to him, and for this reason the people of al-Hira were called al-ʿIbad, because they were people of obedience to the kings of the non-Arabs.

﴿So they denied them, and they became among those destroyed﴾ — by drowning. ﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Book﴾ — the Torah — ﴿so that they might be guided﴾ — so that his people might be guided by it and act upon what is in it. ﴿And We made the son of Maryam and his mother a sign﴾ — a proof of Our power. It should have been stated as "two signs," as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿and We made the night and the day two signs﴾ [Surah al-Isra: 12]. The grammarians differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: its meaning is, "We made each one of them a sign," as He the Exalted says: ﴿Each of the two gardens brought forth its produce﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 33], meaning each one brought forth its produce; and He says ﴿Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are an abomination﴾ [Surah al-Ma'ida: 90], and He did not say "abominations." Others said: its meaning is, "We made their condition one," because ʿIsa was born without a father, and his mother gave birth without any male touching her. ﴿And We gave them refuge on a high ground, a place of stability and flowing water﴾.

Abu Salih Mansur ibn Ahmad al-Mushti informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Razi informed us, saying: Salman ibn ʿAli informed us, saying: Hisham ibn ʿAmmar informed us, saying: ʿAbd al-Majid narrated to us from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted ﴿and We gave them refuge on a high ground, a place of stability and flowing water﴾: he said, "Damascus." Abu Hurayra said: it is al-Ramla. Qatada and Ka'b said: Bayt al-Maqdis. Ka'b said: it is the nearest land to the heaven by eighteen miles. Ibn Zayd said: Egypt. al-Dahhak said: the Ghuta of Damascus. Abu al-ʿAliya said: Iliya, which is the sacred land. By "qarar" is meant a level land and a wide open expanse. And "ma'in" means apparent water visible to the eye of the observer; it is a maf'ul (passive participle form) from ʿanahu, yaʿinahu, when the sight reaches it and sees it. It is also permissible that it be a fa'il form from maʿana, yamʿinu, so it is maʿin, from al-maʿun.

﴿O messengers, eat of the good things﴾ — meaning of the lawful things. The meaning is: and We said to ʿIsa, "Eat of the good things," and this is like saying to a single man in speech, "O people, restrain your harm from us." Its parallels in the Qur'an are numerous. ʿAmr ibn Shurayl said: he used to eat from the spinning of his mother. Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: what is meant by it is Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿And act righteously; indeed, I am Knowing of what you do.﴾ And ﴿Indeed, this your community is one community﴾: the people of Kufa read it with a kasra on the alif, as a new sentence. Ibn ʿAmir read it with a fatha on the alif and a light nun, making inna a connective particle, its meaning being: "And this is your community." The rest read it with a fatha on the alif and a shadda on the nun, meaning "this." It is also permissible that it be in the accusative by an implied verb, meaning: and know that this your community is one community — that is, your religion is one religion, and it is the religion of Islam.

﴿And I am your Lord, so fear Me.﴾ ﴿But they divided their affair among themselves into sects⁠—﴾ The common readers read zuburan with a damma on the ba', meaning books, plural of zabur, in the sense that each group adhered to a book other than the one the other adhered to; this was said by Mujahid and Qatada. It was also said: the meaning is that they divided their religion among themselves into books they invented, arguing for their doctrines through them; this was said by Qatada and Ibn Zayd. The people of Syria read it with a fatha on the ba', meaning pieces and divisions, like the cutting of iron. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Bring me blocks of iron﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 96].

﴿Every faction, with what they have, is pleased.﴾ — each group, with what they have, meaning the religion they hold — ﴿rejoicing﴾: pleased, delighted. ﴿So leave them in their confusion until a time﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: their disbelief and their misguidance. Ibn Zayd: their blindness. Rabi': their heedlessness. ﴿Until a time﴾: until the time of the arrival of their appointed terms.

﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children⁠—﴾ We give them and increase them ﴿—is that We hasten for them in good things?﴾ Its meaning is: Do they suppose that this is hastening for them toward good? ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr read "yusarau" in the passive, but the correct reading is that of the common readers, because of His saying "We extend them." 

﴿Nay, they do not perceive.﴾ That this is an enticement for them. Then He explained who hasten toward good things, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:

﴿Indeed, those who are apprehensive out of fear of their Lord, ﴾ ﴿and those who believe in the signs of their Lord, ﴾ ﴿and those who do not associate anything with their Lord.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 23, verses 60–74:

﴿Those who give what they give﴾: that is, those who give what they have given of the zakat (obligatory alms) and charity (sadaqat). This is the recitation of the people of the major cities (amsar), and it is the reading that their copies of the Qur'an (masahif) follow.

We were informed by Abd al-Khaliq ibn Ali, who said: We were informed by Isma'il ibn Najiyya, who said: Muhammad ibn Ammar ibn Atiyya narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Yazid al-Hulwani narrated to us, who said: Khallad narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn al-Zabarqan, from Muhammad ibn Hammad, from his father, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite ﴿Those who come with what they came with﴾, from "al-majī'" (coming).

We were also informed by al-Hakim Abu Mansur Hamd ibn Ahmad al-Burjani, who said: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Farisi narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl narrated to us, who said: Abu Usama narrated to us, who said: Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to me, who said:

I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani mention that Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "O Messenger of Allah,

﴿Those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful, because they will return to their Lord﴾, is it the one who commits adultery and drinks wine, while he fears Allah?" He said: "No, O daughter of the Truthful (al-Siddiq), rather it is the one who fasts, prays and gives charity, while he fears Allah, glorified is He."

[Musnad al-Humaydi: 1/133, with variation.]

We were also informed by Abdullah ibn Yusuf, who said: Muhammad ibn Hamid narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm narrated to us, who said: Abdullah ibn Amr narrated to us, who said: Waki' informed us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id ibn Wahb, from Aisha, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, ﴿Those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful﴾, is it the one who commits adultery, drinks wine and steals?" He said: "No, O daughter of Abu Bakr, or O daughter of the Truthful, rather it is the man who fasts, prays and gives charity, and fears that it will not be accepted from him."

[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 18/45.]

﴿Those are they who hasten to the good deeds, and they are foremost in them﴾: that is, "to them" (ilayha), like the Qur'anic expressions ﴿for what they were forbidden﴾ and ﴿for what they said﴾ and similar. Ibn Abbas used to say concerning the meaning of this verse: "Happiness had already been decreed for them by Allah, and that is why they hastened to the good deeds."

﴿And We do not burden any soul except within its capacity﴾: that is, only what it can bear and what is suitable for it of worship and law.

﴿And with Us is a Book that speaks with the truth﴾: that is, the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), which clarifies with truth what they did and what they will do of good and evil. It was also said: it is the book of the deeds of the servants, which the guardian angels (al-hafaza) record, and this is more fitting to the apparent meaning of the verse.

﴿And they will not be wronged﴾: that is, they will be given the full recompense for their deeds, neither their good deeds being diminished nor their evil deeds being increased.

Then He mentioned the disbelievers, so the Mighty One said:

﴿Rather, their hearts are in confusion﴾ concerning ﴿this Qur'an﴾: meaning blindness and heedlessness. ﴿And they have deeds other than that﴾: evil deeds that Allah does not approve of, of sins and transgressions. ﴿Other than that﴾ means other than the deeds of the believers that Allah, glorified is He, mentioned. It was said: those deeds are His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are apprehensive out of fear of their Lord﴾.

﴿They will continue to do them﴾: they must inevitably do them, and so they will enter the Fire by them, because of the wretchedness decreed for them.

﴿Until when We seize their affluent ones﴾: that is, their wealthy ones and leaders ﴿with punishment﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "With the swords on the Day of Badr."

Al-Dahhak said: it means hunger, and that was when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invoked against them, saying: "O Allah, tighten Your grip on Mudar, and make it upon them years like the years of Yusuf." So Allah afflicted them with famine until they ate carrion, dogs, burnt bones, hides and children.

[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 7/199.]

﴿Then, when they will cry out﴾: they will wail, lament and implore. The origin of al-ju'ar is raising the voice in supplication, as a bull does. The poet said:

"She circled for three days, between a day and a night,
and the denial was that she should host and cry out."

He describes a cow. And he also said:

"He alternates between the prayers to the King,
at times prostrating, at times crying out."

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 12/135. The phrase is given as "yurawih".]

﴿Do not cry out today; indeed, you will not be helped﴾: you will not be protected, and your lamenting and supplication will not benefit you.

﴿My verses were already recited to you﴾: meaning the Qur'an, ﴿but you turned back on your heels﴾: on your backs, ﴿retreating﴾, meaning you reflected and drew back, and withdrew, turning backward, denying them and disliking them, ﴿arrogant about it﴾: that is, about the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram). You say: "No one will prevail over us, for we are the people of the Haram." And this is a metaphor for something unmentioned.

﴿Sāmiran﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal): meaning that they would hold nighttime conversations (yasmuruna) in their gatherings around the House. And He used the singular "sāmiran," though it carries the sense of the plural "sumar" (evening talkers), because it was placed in the position of a time expression. The intended meaning is: ﴿deserting [it] by night﴾, like the poet's saying:

"Beyond them, if you come to them at night (sumaran),
is the sound of singing-girls and a noisy gathering."

He said "sumaran" because its meaning is: "if you come to them at night while they are conversing." It was also said that it is singular with a plural meaning, as in His saying: ﴿Then He brings you out as infants﴾ and similar.

﴿Tahjurūn﴾: Nafi' recited it with a dammah on the ta' and a kasrah on the jim, meaning "you utter obscenities and say abusive speech." It is said: "ahjara al-rajul" meaning he spoke obscenely. It is reported that they used to revile the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions. The rest of the reciters read it with a fathah on the ta' and a dammah on the jim, and it has two possible meanings:

First: you turn away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Qur'an and faith, and reject them.

﴿Those who give what they give﴾: that is, those who give what they have given of the zakat (obligatory alms) and charity (sadaqat). This is the recitation of the people of the major cities (amsar), and it is the reading that their copies of the Qur'an (masahif) follow.

We were informed by Abd al-Khaliq ibn Ali, who said: We were informed by Isma'il ibn Najiyya, who said: Muhammad ibn Ammar ibn Atiyya narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Yazid al-Hulwani narrated to us, who said: Khallad narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn al-Zabarqan, from Muhammad ibn Hammad, from his father, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite ﴿Those who come with what they came with﴾, from "al-majī'" (coming).

We were also informed by al-Hakim Abu Mansur Hamd ibn Ahmad al-Burjani, who said: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa al-Farisi narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl narrated to us, who said: Abu Usama narrated to us, who said: Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to me, who said:

I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani mention that Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "O Messenger of Allah,

﴿Those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful, because they will return to their Lord﴾, is it the one who commits adultery and drinks wine, while he fears Allah?" He said: "No, O daughter of the Truthful (al-Siddiq), rather it is the one who fasts, prays and gives charity, while he fears Allah, glorified is He."

[Musnad al-Humaydi: 1/133, with variation.]

We were also informed by Abdullah ibn Yusuf, who said: Muhammad ibn Hamid narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm narrated to us, who said: Abdullah ibn Amr narrated to us, who said: Waki' informed us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id ibn Wahb, from Aisha, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, ﴿Those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful﴾, is it the one who commits adultery, drinks wine and steals?" He said: "No, O daughter of Abu Bakr, or O daughter of the Truthful, rather it is the man who fasts, prays and gives charity, and fears that it will not be accepted from him."

[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 18/45.]

﴿Those are they who hasten to the good deeds, and they are foremost in them﴾: that is, "to them" (ilayha), like the Qur'anic expressions ﴿for what they were forbidden﴾ and ﴿for what they said﴾ and similar. Ibn Abbas used to say concerning the meaning of this verse: "Happiness had already been decreed for them by Allah, and that is why they hastened to the good deeds."

﴿And We do not burden any soul except within its capacity﴾: that is, only what it can bear and what is suitable for it of worship and law.

﴿And with Us is a Book that speaks with the truth﴾: that is, the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), which clarifies with truth what they did and what they will do of good and evil. It was also said: it is the book of the deeds of the servants, which the guardian angels (al-hafaza) record, and this is more fitting to the apparent meaning of the verse.

﴿And they will not be wronged﴾: that is, they will be given the full recompense for their deeds, neither their good deeds being diminished nor their evil deeds being increased.

Then He mentioned the disbelievers, so the Mighty One said:

﴿Rather, their hearts are in confusion﴾ concerning ﴿this Qur'an﴾: meaning blindness and heedlessness. ﴿And they have deeds other than that﴾: evil deeds that Allah does not approve of, of sins and transgressions. ﴿Other than that﴾ means other than the deeds of the believers that Allah, glorified is He, mentioned. It was said: those deeds are His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are apprehensive out of fear of their Lord﴾.

﴿They will continue to do them﴾: they must inevitably do them, and so they will enter the Fire by them, because of the wretchedness decreed for them.

﴿Until when We seize their affluent ones﴾: that is, their wealthy ones and leaders ﴿with punishment﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "With the swords on the Day of Badr."

Al-Dahhak said: it means hunger, and that was when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invoked against them, saying: "O Allah, tighten Your grip on Mudar, and make it upon them years like the years of Yusuf." So Allah afflicted them with famine until they ate carrion, dogs, burnt bones, hides and children.

[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 7/199.]

﴿Then, when they will cry out﴾: they will wail, lament and implore. The origin of al-ju'ar is raising the voice in supplication, as a bull does. The poet said:

"She circled for three days, between a day and a night,
and the denial was that she should host and cry out."

He describes a cow. And he also said:

"He alternates between the prayers to the King,
at times prostrating, at times crying out."

[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 12/135. The phrase is given as "yurawih".]

﴿Do not cry out today; indeed, you will not be helped﴾: you will not be protected, and your lamenting and supplication will not benefit you.

﴿My verses were already recited to you﴾: meaning the Qur'an, ﴿but you turned back on your heels﴾: on your backs, ﴿retreating﴾, meaning you reflected and drew back, and withdrew, turning backward, denying them and disliking them, ﴿arrogant about it﴾: that is, about the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram). And He used the singular "sāmiran," though it carries the sense of the plural "sumar" (evening talkers), because it was placed in the position of a time expression. The intended meaning is: ﴿deserting [it] by night﴾, like the poet's saying:

"Beyond them, if you come to them at night (sumaran),
is the sound of singing-girls and a noisy gathering."

He said "sumaran" because its meaning is: "if you come to them at night while they are conversing." It was also said that it is singular with a plural meaning, as in His saying: ﴿Then He brings you out as infants﴾ and similar.

﴿Tahjurūn﴾: Nafi' recited it with a dammah on the ta' and a kasrah on the jim, meaning "you utter obscenities and say abusive speech." It is said: "ahjara al-rajul" meaning he spoke obscenely. Ibn 'Abbas said: When Thumama ibn Uthal al-Hanafi came to the Prophet (ﷺ), he embraced Islam while he was a captive, so the Prophet released him. He then went to al-Yamamah and cut off the supply of produce from al-Yamamah to the people of Makkah. God then struck Quraysh (in another copy: "whomever He willed" instead of "Quraysh") with years of drought until they ate al-'Ilhiz (a paste made of blood and hair). Abu Sufyan then came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I implore you by God and by kinship: do you not claim that you were sent as a mercy to the worlds?" He said: "Yes." He said: "You have killed the fathers by the sword and the sons by hunger." So God revealed this verse: ﴿Until, when We open for them a gate of severe punishment,﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: this refers to the Day of Badr. Mujahid said: it refers to the famine. It was also said: it refers to the punishment of the Fire in the Hereafter. ﴿Then they will be in despair,﴾ ﴿mubliswn (in despair)﴾: bewildered, hopeless of every good.

﴿And it is He who produced for you hearing, sight and hearts; little is it that you give thanks.﴾ ﴿And it is He who multiplied you upon the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.﴾ ﴿And it is He who gives life and causes death, and His is the alternation of the night and the day. Will you not then reason?﴾ ﴿Nay, they say the like of what the former ones said.﴾ ﴿They said: "When we are dead and have become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?﴾ ﴿Indeed we were promised this, we and our fathers before. This is nothing but the fables of the ancients.﴾ The promise made to us and to our fathers before us: some people claimed that they were prophets of God, but no reality was found in that.

﴿Say, O Muhammad, answering them: "To whom belong the earth and whoever is in it, if you know?"﴾ ﴿They will say: "To God."﴾ They must say this, so say to them when they acknowledge it: ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾ so that you may know that the One who was able to create it at the beginning is able to bring it back to life after their death.

﴿Say: "Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Mighty Throne?"﴾ ﴿They will say: "God."﴾

The majority of readers recited: "lillah (to God)," and what follows it likewise. They made the answer conform to the meaning rather than to the wording, like one who says to a man: "Whose client are you?" and he replies: "To so-and-so," meaning: "I belong to so-and-so, and he is my patron." And the poet recited:

"And know that I will become a grave, when the camels pass by and do not stop."

When the askers said: "For whom have you dug?" the informers replied: "A minister for them."

Here the genitive was answered with a nominative, because the meaning of the statement is: "The askers said: 'Who is the dead man?' The informers said: 'The dead man is a minister,'" so he answered the meaning. Another said:

"If it is said, 'Who is the lord of the estates and the villages, and the lord of the swift noble horses?' it is said: 'Khalid.'"

Al-Akhfash said: the lam is extra, meaning "Allah." The people of Basra read both as "Allah" with an alif, which is clear and needs no interpretation. In the codices of all the cities it is "lillah," except in the codex of the people of Basra, where it is "Allah Allah," so each followed its own codex. They did not differ regarding the first, that it is "lillah," because it is written without an alif in all the codices, and it is an answer that matches the question in ﴿To whom belong the earth and whoever is in it﴾, so its answer is "lillah" ...

﴿Will you not then fear God, and obey Him?﴾ ﴿Say: "In whose hand is the dominion of everything,"﴾ meaning His possession and treasuries. ﴿And He gives protection, but no one can be protected against Him,﴾ meaning He grants safety to whom He wills, and no one can protect whom He fears. ﴿If you know.﴾ The people of meanings said: the sense is, "Answer, if you know."

﴿They will say: "To God."﴾ ﴿Say: "How then are you deluded?"﴾ meaning: you are deceived and turned away from His oneness and obedience.

﴿Rather, We have brought them the truth, and they are indeed liars.﴾ ﴿God has not taken a son, and there is not with Him any god; otherwise each god would have taken away what he created, and they would have overcome one another, and the stronger of them would have prevailed over the weaker.﴾ ﴿Glory be to God above what they describe,﴾ of lies. ﴿Knower of the unseen and the visible,﴾ with the genitive: Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Abu 'Amr read it as an adjective of God. Others read it in the nominative, as a new subject or meaning "He is the Knower."

Ruways narrated from Ya'qub that when he began a recitation he used the nominative, and when he joined it to what followed he used the genitive.

﴿Exalted is He above what they associate.﴾

﴿Say: "My Lord, if You show me that which they are promised,"﴾ of punishment, ﴿"My Lord, do not place me among the wrongdoing people,"﴾ meaning do not destroy me with their destruction. The fa' in His words ﴿fa-la (then do not)﴾ is not the answer to amma (if), because it is a condition and its consequence.

﴿And We are able to show you what We promise them,﴾ of punishment, so We have made it for them. ﴿Repel evil with that which is better,﴾ meaning with the trait that is better: ﴿al-sayyi'ah (evil)﴾ is their harm and their harshness. He says: turn away from their harm and pardon them. It was abrogated by the verse of fighting (naskh, abrogation).

﴿We know best what they describe,﴾ so We will recompense them for it. ﴿And say: "My Lord, I seek refuge with You﴾ ﴿from the whisperings of the devils,"﴾ meaning their incitements. This is from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Hasan said: their whisperings. Mujahid said: their blowing and spitting. Ibn Zayd said: their choking of people.

The people of meanings said: it means their pushing toward sins through seduction. Hamz means a strong push, and from it the letter produced by the breath of the mouth in pushing is called hamzah.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (*al-Jawahir al-Hisan*) on surah 23 (al-Mu'minun), verses 99–111:

﴿Until, when death comes to one of them﴾: meaning these polytheists. This happens when he is cut off from the world and witnesses the Hereafter, before he tastes death.

﴿He says, "My Lord, send me back."﴾ He did not say "send me back" (irji'ni) in the singular but "send me back" (irji'un) in the plural, which is the address of one person in honour, like His saying ﴿Indeed, We, We﴾. So he was addressed in this way, just as He began with the expression of honour.

Some of them said: this request was made by them to the angels who take their souls. The speech began with the address to God, Glorified, because they first sought help from God, Glorified, and then turned to the request of the angels to return to the world.

﴿So that I may do righteousness in what I have left behind.﴾ "Left behind" means "neglected." ﴿No!﴾ means he will not return to it. It is a word of restraint and rebuke. ﴿It is only a word he says﴾: meaning his request to return, and he will not attain it.

Aishah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When the believer witnesses the angels, they say: 'Shall we return you to the world?' He says: 'To the abode of worries and sorrows? No, but send me forward to God, Mighty and Majestic.' As for the disbeliever, he says, ﴿My Lord, send me back﴾, the verse." [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 18/68.]

﴿And behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected.﴾ Behind them means in front of them. A barrier means a hindrance between death and the return to the world. This is from Mujahid. Ibn 'Abbas said: a partition. Al-Suddi said: a term. Qatadah said: the remainder of the world. Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: what lies between death and resurrection. Abu Umamah said: the grave. It was also said: a reprieve. [In the second copy there is an addition: "Every separation between two things is a barrier." The words of God, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿Then when the Horn is blown, there will be no kinship between them﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said.] They will not boast of lineages in the Hereafter as they used to boast [In the second copy there is an addition: "in the world."].

﴿Then when the Horn is blown, there will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask of one another.﴾

Abu al-'Aliyah said: this is like His saying ﴿And no close friend will ask about a close friend﴾.

Ibn Jurayj said: the meaning of the verse is that no one that Day will ask another about lineage, ﴿nor will they ask of one another﴾, meaning no one will claim kinship through a relative.

The exegetes differed concerning what is meant by His saying ﴿when the Horn is blown﴾: which of the two blasts is intended? Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the first blast.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me by my reading to him, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Ibrahim ibn Ayyub told us, saying: Abu 'Abdullah Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Awf told us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Ubayd ibn Abi Karimah al-Harrani told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salamah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahim told us, saying: Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah narrated to me from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying, Glorified be He, ﴿there will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask of one another﴾: this is at the first blast. ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom God wills﴾ [Surah al-Zumar: 68]. ﴿So there will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask of one another﴾ [Surah al-Mu'minun: 101]. ﴿Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on﴾ [Surah al-Zumar: 68]. ﴿And some of them will turn to others, asking one another﴾ [Surah al-Saffat: 27].

Ibn Mas'ud said: it is the second blast.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shaybah told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi told us, saying: Yazid ibn Mawhab al-Ramli told us, saying: 'Isa ibn Yunus told us, from Harun ibn Abi Wakee', who said: I heard Zadhan Abu 'Umar say: I entered upon Ibn Mas'ud and found the people of silk (khazz) and Yemeni cloaks had preceded me to the gatherings. So I called to him: "O 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud! Because I am a non-Arab man, you brought them near and pushed me away?" He said: "Come near." So I came near until there was no one sitting between me and him. I heard him say: "On the Day of Resurrection, a male or female slave will be taken by the hand and placed before the first and the last. Then a herald will call out: 'This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so. Whoever has a right against him, let him come to his right.' The woman will rejoice when her right is claimed from her father, or her husband, or her son, or her sister." Then Ibn Mas'ud recited ﴿So there will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask of one another﴾ and said: "God, Glorified be He, will say: 'Give these people their rights.' He will say: 'My Lord, the world has perished.' He will say to the angels: 'Take from his deeds and give each person according to his claim. If he was a friend of God, Mighty and Majestic, and his good deeds exceed by the weight of a mustard seed, He will multiply it for him until He admits him to Paradise by it.'" Then Ibn Mas'ud recited ﴿Indeed, God does not wrong [even] the weight of an atom; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 40]. [In the second copy there is an addition: ﴿and gives from Himself a great reward﴾.] "But if he was wretched, the angels will say: 'My Lord, his good deeds have perished and there remain claimants.' He will say: 'Take from their evil deeds and add them to his evil deeds, and write for him a writ to the Fire.'"

﴿As for those whose scales are heavy, they are the successful. And as for those whose scales are light, they are the ones who have lost themselves, remaining forever in Hell.﴾ ﴿The Fire will scorch their faces, and they therein will be grim-faced﴾: it scorches (tasfa'). Grim-faced means scowling. This is from Ibn 'Abbas. Others said: the kalh is when the two lips draw back from a person until the teeth show.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Have you not seen the head scorched by fire, its teeth showing and its lips drawn back?"

Al-A'sha said:
"He has the foremost place, with no equal,
at the hour when the jaw recoils from the fang, grimacing."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan ibn 'Abdullah told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Masuhi told us, saying: Yahya al-Hammani told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, from Sa'id ibn Yazid Abu Shuja', from Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿The Fire will scorch their faces, and they therein will be grim-faced﴾. He said: "The Fire burns them, so that the upper lip shrinks until it reaches the middle of the head, and the lower lip slackens until it reaches the navel." [Musnad Ahmad: 3/88.]

﴿Were not My verses recited to you, and you used to deny them?﴾ ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a people astray."﴾ "Our wretchedness" that was decreed for us. The people of Kufa except 'Asim read shaqawatuna with an alif and a fatha on the shin. Others read shiqwatuna without alif and with a kasra on the shin. Both are dialectal forms. It means the harm that befalls one in the end, while happiness is the benefit that befalls one in the end.

﴿Our Lord, bring us out of it. If we return, then we are indeed wrongdoers.﴾ That is, from the Fire, or from what You dislike. They will be answered after a thousand years: ﴿Remain in it in disgrace, and do not speak to Me.﴾ That is, be gone, as one says to a dog: "Ikhsa'!" when it is driven away and sent off. ﴿And do not speak to Me﴾ regarding lifting the punishment, for I will not lift it from you nor lighten it for you. It was also said: this is an indication of the lasting anger upon them. At that point the wretched ones despaired of relief.

Al-Hasan said: this is the last speech spoken by the people of the Fire. After it they will speak no more except sighing and groaning, and their cry will become like the howling of a dog, which they neither understand nor are understood.

﴿Indeed, there was a group of My servants﴾: this ha' (the pronoun) is an auxiliary and is also called the unknown (al-majhulah). They are the believers. ﴿who said, "Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful." But you took them in derision﴾. The people of Medina and Kufa, except 'Asim, read sukhriyyan with a damma on the sin here and in surah Sad. The rest read it with a kasra.

Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: both are dialects, like the Arabs' saying: bahr lujjiyy and lujji (deep sea), and kawkab durriyy and durri (a bright star), and kursiyy and kursi (a throne).

Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' said: the kasr means mockery by speech, and the damm means subjugation and enslavement in action. They did not differ that in surah al-Zukhruf it is with damm, because it means subjugation and enslavement, except what was narrated from Ibn Muhaysin that he read it with a kasra by analogy to the rest, but this is not strong.

﴿Until they made you forget My remembrance﴾: that is, your preoccupation with mocking them and subjugating them made you forget My remembrance. ﴿And you used to laugh at them.﴾ A parallel to His saying, Glorified be He: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed﴾ [Surah al-Mutaffifin: 29].

﴿Indeed, I have rewarded them today for what they endured﴾: for their patience under your mockery of them in the world. Recompense is the matching of an action with what it deserves of reward or punishment.

﴿That they are the triumphant.﴾ Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read innahum with a kasra on the alif as a new sentence. The rest read it with a fatha, meaning "because they are the triumphant." It may also be in the accusative by the falling of the recompense upon it: ﴿Indeed, I have rewarded them today﴾, the triumph of Paradise.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Have you not seen the head scorched by fire, its teeth showing and its lips drawn back?"

Al-A'sha said:
"He has the foremost place, with no equal,

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (*al-Jawahir al-Hisan*) on surah 23 (al-Mu'minun), verses 99–111:

﴿Until, when death comes to one of them﴾: meaning these polytheists. This happens when he is cut off from the world and witnesses the Hereafter, before he tastes death.

﴿He says, "My Lord, send me back."﴾ He did not say "send me back" (irji'ni) in the singular but "send me back" (irji'un) in the plural, which is the address of one person in honour, like His saying ﴿Indeed, We, We﴾. So he was addressed in this way, just as He began with the expression of honour.

Some of them said: this request was made by them to the angels who take their souls. The speech began with the address to God, Glorified, because they first sought help from God, Glorified, and then turned to the request of the angels to return to the world.

﴿So that I may do righteousness in what I have left behind.﴾ "Left behind" means "neglected." ﴿No!﴾ means he will not return to it. It is a word of restraint and rebuke. ﴿It is only a word he says﴾: meaning his request to return, and he will not attain it.

Aishah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When the believer witnesses the angels, they say: 'Shall we return you to the world?' He says: 'To the abode of worries and sorrows? No, but send me forward to God, Mighty and Majestic.' As for the disbeliever, he says, ﴿My Lord, send me back﴾, the verse." [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 18/68.]

Abu al-'Aliyah said: this is like His saying ﴿And no close friend will ask about a close friend﴾.

Ibn Jurayj said: the meaning of the verse is that no one that Day will ask another about lineage, ﴿nor will they ask of one another﴾, meaning no one will claim kinship through a relative.

**Section on the wisdoms behind God's creation of creatures**

The scholars who investigate said: God, glory be to Him, created creation in order to show by that His existence and the perfection of His knowledge and power, for if He had not created, His existence would have no meaning.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Mansur ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: I said to al-Hasan al-Basri, concerning His words, glory be to Him: ﴿And they will not cease to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy﴾.³

He said: "People differ in various religions, except those on whom your Lord has mercy, and those on whom your Lord has mercy do not differ."

It was said to him: "And for that He created them?"

He said: "Yes. He created these for His Paradise and He created these for His Fire, He created these for His mercy and He created these for His punishment."

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Faqih informed us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Musa al-Faqih informed us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi narrated to us, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Nasr, who said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad was asked: "Why did God create creation?"

He said: "Because God, glory be to Him, was ever beneficent in what has never ceased, in what has never ceased. He wished, glory be to Him and exalted, to entrust His beneficence to His creatures, while He was independent of them. He did not create them to bring about any benefit, nor to repel any harm, but He created them, did good to them, and sent to them messengers so that they might distinguish between truth and falsehood. Whoever does good, He rewards with Paradise, and whoever disobeys, He recompenses with the Fire."

Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi said: God, glory be to Him, created creatures as servants so that they would worship Him, and He rewards them for servitude and punishes them for abandoning it. If they worship Him, they are today noble, free servants, and tomorrow they are free and kings in the Abode of Peace. If they reject servitude, they are today runaway, base and vile slaves, and tomorrow they are enemies in prisons among the layers of the Fires.

Among them is one who said: God, glory be to Him, created all creatures for the sake of Muhammad ﷺ. This is shown by what Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn al-Rumi narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Hamdun ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn al-'Abbas al-Hashimi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yasin ibn Shurayk narrated to us, saying: Jandal narrated to us, saying:

'Amr ibn Aws al-Ansari narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "God, glory be to Him, revealed to 'Isa (peace be upon him): 'O 'Isa, believe in Muhammad, and order your nation to believe in him. Had it not been for Muhammad, I would not have created Adam. Had it not been for Muhammad, I would not have created Paradise and Hellfire. I created the Throne upon the water, and it trembled, so I wrote upon it: There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God ﷺ, and it became still.'"⁴

I heard Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Farisi say: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Bahram al-Farisi say: I heard al-Qannad [in the second copy (Isfahan): al-'Abbad] say: "God, glory be to Him, created the angels for power, and created things for lesson [in the second copy: for deception], and created you for love of Him." Among the scholars is one who did not state this explicitly, but said: God, glory be to Him, drew attention in more than one place in His revealed Books that He created them for a great matter that is hidden from them, which will not be made clear until what He created them for befalls them. This is the meaning of His words, glory be to Him: ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose?﴾, and the verse.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Baghawi narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Rashid narrated to us. And Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muris [in the second copy: Quraysh] informed us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Hubayrah, from Hanash [in the second copy: Jaysh] ibn 'Abd Allah al-San'ani, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, that he passed by a afflicted sufferer and recited into his ear ﴿Did you think that We created you without purpose?﴾ until he finished the surah, and he was cured. The Messenger of God ﷺ said to him: "What did you recite into his ear?" He told him, and he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if a man of certainty recited it upon a mountain, it would move."⁵

Then He declared Himself free of what the polytheists attributed to Him of taking rivals and offspring, and what the atheists ascribed to Him of folly and aimlessness. He, the Mighty, said: ﴿So exalted is God, the true King. There is no god but Him, Lord of the Noble Throne.﴾ That is, the great, magnificent Throne. ﴿And whoever calls upon another god along with God, for which he has no proof—his account is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.﴾ The scholars of meanings said: there is an implied element in it; its sense is: "then he has no proof for it." ﴿And say, "My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful."﴾
